notes: **Definition:** delocalization of pi electrons or lone pairs through resonance, transmitting electron density through conjugated systems.
**+R effect (electron donating):** groups with lone pairs donate electron density into the pi system. Examples: $-OH$, $-OR$, $-NH_2$, $-NHR$, $-NR_2$.
**-R effect (electron withdrawing):** groups with multiple bonds to electronegative atoms withdraw electron density. Examples: $-NO_2$, $-CN$, $-COOH$, $-SO_3H$, $-CHO$, $-COR$.
**Comparison with inductive effect:** resonance effect is much stronger than inductive effect but operates only through conjugated pi systems. Inductive effect operates through sigma bonds.

**Effect on reactivity:** +R groups activate aromatic rings toward electrophilic substitution; -R groups deactivate. Example: aniline reacts faster than benzene because $-NH_2$ donates electrons by resonance.
